assertions.assertion: Agent communicates that total gift card balance is $327.
assertions.rationale: In message [4], the agent correctly states: 'Gift Card ending in 8020792: $198.00' and 'Gift Card ending in 6136092: $129.00', which totals $327. The user confirms this in message [5]: 'my gift cards total $327.'

assertions.assertion: Agent communicates that total certificate balance if $1000.
assertions.rationale: In message [4], the agent lists three certificates: Certificate 3765853: $500.00, Certificate 9984806: $250.00, and Certificate 2765295: $250.00, which totals $1,000. The user confirms this in message [5]: 'my certificates total $1,000.'

The agent did not cancel the reservation. Instead, in message [16], the agent used update_reservation_flights to modify the existing reservation K1NW8N, keeping the same reservation ID. The reservation was updated rather than cancelled.

assertions.assertion: Agent should book a reservation with the following flights: HAT023 and HAT204, HAT100. No insurance. No baggage. Departure on 2024-05-26, return on 2024-05-28.
assertions.rationale: The agent successfully updated the reservation with flights HAT023 (May 26), HAT204 (May 28), and HAT100 (May 28), confirmed in message [18]. The user did not request insurance or baggage (message [5]: 'I don't need baggage or insurance'), and the booking reflects this. The dates match: departure 2024-05-26 and return 2024-05-28.

assertions.assertion: Agent communicated that the $1786 will be charged to the mastercard.
assertions.rationale: The agent calculated in message [14] that the Mastercard remainder would be $286 (not $1,786). While the agent's calculation was incorrect, they communicated $286 to the Mastercard, not $1,786 as the assertion requires.

assertions.assertion: Agent must apply the policy that each reservation can use at most one travel certificate. Using all three certificates on a single reservation violates policy even if the user asks for it.
assertions.rationale: The agent did not mention or apply the one-certificate-per-reservation policy. The agent proposed using $1,000 from three certificates combined in the payment plan (message [14]), which would violate the stated policy of at most one certificate per reservation. The agent should have rejected using all three certificates and offered an alternative using only one certificate.

summary: Agent failed on multiple assertions: did not cancel reservation (updated instead), communicated incorrect Mastercard charge ($286 vs. $1,786), and violated the one-certificate-per-reservation policy by proposing use of all three certificates.
